$comment: Category explorer data. Edit this file to add/change taxonomy dimensions, their descriptions, and value summaries. Paper references for each value are computed automatically from papers.json (do not edit those).
intro: This page explains how the 53 reviewed papers were classified across the taxonomy of the systematic literature review. Each dimension below groups related categories; every category lists the papers that were classified with it. Click the arrow on a category to see its references.

dimensions.label: Research Type
dimensions.description: Whether a study's primary objective is to develop or evaluate XUQ methods (method-oriented) or to apply XUQ to a specific domain problem (application-oriented).

values.summary: XUQ is applied to address a specific problem within an application domain.
The study develops, extends, or evaluates XUQ methods.

dimensions.label: Application Domain
dimensions.description: The real-world application domain in which XUQ is employed (for application-oriented studies).

values.summary: XUQ applied to medical and clinical decision support.
XUQ applied to environmental modelling and monitoring.
XUQ applied to industrial processes and engineering.
XUQ applied to autonomous driving perception and control.
XUQ applied to remote sensing and earth observation.
XUQ applied to chemical and molecular property prediction.
XUQ applied to energy systems and forecasting.
XUQ applied to civil engineering and infrastructure.
XUQ applied to aviation and aerospace.
XUQ applied to cybersecurity and side-channel analysis.

dimensions.label: Data Modality
dimensions.description: The type of data the XUQ method operates on.

values.summary: XUQ applied to image data.
XUQ applied to tabular / structured data.
XUQ applied to time series data.
XUQ applied to text data.
XUQ applied to graph-structured data.
XUQ applied to structured spatiotemporal data.
XUQ applied to multimodal data.
XUQ applied to event data.

dimensions.label: ML Task
dimensions.description: The machine learning problem class addressed by the study.

values.summary: XUQ applied to classification tasks.
XUQ applied to regression tasks.
XUQ applied to time series forecasting.
XUQ applied to trajectory prediction.
XUQ applied to segmentation tasks.
XUQ applied to object detection.

dimensions.label: Audience
dimensions.description: The intended target audience of the explanations, if mentioned.

values.summary: Explanations intended for domain experts.
Explanations intended for ML researchers and engineers.
Explanations intended for lay or end users.
Explanations intended for data labelers.
No target audience specified.

dimensions.label: Uncertainty Type
dimensions.description: The type of uncertainty that is explained.

values.summary: Overall predictive uncertainty (aleatoric + epistemic).
Uncertainty due to the model's lack of knowledge.
Irreducible uncertainty inherent in the data.
Other or composite uncertainty types.
The uncertainty type is not specified.

dimensions.label: UQ Method
dimensions.description: The method used to generate the uncertainty estimate, grouped into the paper's taxonomy categories.

values.summary: Uncertainty from disagreement across multiple model instances or stochastic inference runs (e.g. MC dropout, deep ensembles, tree-based ensembles).
Uncertainty from explicitly modelling probability distributions over parameters or predictions (e.g. BNNs, Gaussian processes, evidential deep learning).
Uncertainty derived directly from the model's deterministic outputs, typically the softmax confidence or entropy.
Uncertainty quantified without parametric assumptions about the predictive distribution (e.g. conformal prediction, quantile regression).
Uncertainty based on the position or similarity of a sample within a learned representation space (e.g. prototypes, VAEs).
Other or unspecified UQ methods (e.g. fuzzy logic systems).

dimensions.label: Uncertainty Estimate
dimensions.description: The specific uncertainty estimate that is explained.

values.summary: Uncertainty quantified as entropy of predictions.
Uncertainty quantified as variance or standard deviation.
Uncertainty quantified via prediction intervals or quantiles.
Uncertainty quantified as a parameter of a predicted distribution.
Uncertainty quantified as a probability or confidence score.
Uncertainty quantified via distance-based measures.
The uncertainty estimate is not specified or unclear.

dimensions.label: Integration Type
dimensions.description: How the explanation is integrated with the model and UQ mechanism.

values.summary: Explanation applied after training, without changing the model.
Explanation retrieved directly from the model or UQ mechanism.
Combination of post-hoc and intrinsic elements.

dimensions.label: Portability
dimensions.description: Whether the XUQ method applies to any model or only specific ones.

values.summary: Applicable to any black-box model.
Restricted to a specific model class or architecture.

dimensions.label: Locality
dimensions.description: Whether the explanation is specific to an instance or global to the model.

values.summary: Explanation specific to a single prediction.
Explanation of overall model behaviour.
Provides both local and global explanations.
Uncertainty attributed to input features.
Minimal input changes that alter the uncertainty.
Explanation in terms of higher-level concepts.
Explanation as explicit human-readable rules.
Explanation via similar or influential examples.
Other or unspecified explanation output types.

dimensions.label: Evaluated
dimensions.description: Whether the study evaluated its explanations of uncertainty.

values.summary: The explanations were evaluated in some form.
The explanations were not evaluated.
Evaluation using quantitative proxy metrics.
Evaluation via user studies with humans.
Evaluation via anecdotal visual inspection.
How faithful the explanation is to the model.
How plausible the explanation is to users.
How relevant the explanation is to the user's needs.
How continuous / robust the explanation function is.
How sparse and concise the explanation is.
How deterministic the explanation is.

dimensions.label: Benchmarked
dimensions.description: Whether the XUQ method was compared against other methods.

values.summary: The method was benchmarked against other approaches.
The method was not benchmarked.

dimensions.label: SHAP
dimensions.description: Whether SHAP was used as the attribution method.

values.summary: SHAP was used to explain the uncertainty.
